name: Data lineage LPG (PROV-inspired)
description: Labeled property graph ontology for data lineage, inspired by the W3C PROV-O vocabulary. It is not a PROV-O serialization and does not promise a round trip to RDF: references to PROV terms point to the closest concept, not to an equivalence. Logical objects (Dataset, Column, Job) are stable over time; versions (DatasetVersion, ColumnVersion, JobVersion) are immutable and carry the lineage, so questions can be asked as of a point in time. Run-level facts (USED, WAS_GENERATED_BY) record what a run read and wrote. They do not mean that every output depends on every input. Asserted derivations (WAS_DERIVED_FROM, COLUMN_DERIVED_FROM) come from a named source such as OpenLineage column lineage, a SQL parser or a dbt manifest. Potential dependencies computed from run inputs and outputs are stored separately as DEPENDS_ON. Time: generatedAt is when a version was produced, publishedAt when it was exposed to consumers, validFrom and validTo when it is the version consumers should see. Point-in-time queries use validFrom and validTo, not generatedAt alone. Invalidation never deletes history. Cross-level consistency rules described on relationships, such as a column version belonging to a version of the column's own dataset, are enforced by ingestion; the format cannot express them. KEY and existence constraints require Neo4j Enterprise Edition or Aura.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:0.description: Base label for everything that has lineage: datasets, columns, jobs and their versions. Abstract by convention (not a field of the format): every Entity node also carries a more specific label. Holds the id uniqueness constraint shared by all subtypes.

p:1.name: id
p:1.description: Stable identifier, unique across all activities.

n:1.description: Base label for things that happen over time and read or write entities. Abstract by convention: every Activity node also carries a more specific label, such as Run.

p:2.name: id
p:2.description: Stable identifier, unique across all agents.

n:2.description: Base label for people, software and organizations that are responsible for runs or own assets. Abstract by convention: every Agent node also carries a more specific label.

p:4.name: id
p:4.description: Stable identifier, for example ds:snowflake://acme/stg.orders. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:5.name: namespace
p:5.description: Namespace of the data source, for example snowflake://acme or postgres://db1:5432. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.

p:6.name: name
p:6.description: Name of the dataset within its namespace, for example stg.orders. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.

p:7.name: system
p:7.description: System that hosts the dataset, for example snowflake.

p:9.name: retiredAt
p:9.description: When the dataset was logically retired. Retirement does not delete its versions or lineage.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:3.description: The logical asset, stable over time: a table, topic, file, model or dashboard. Identified by namespace and name, as in OpenLineage. Lineage attaches to its versions, not to it directly.

p:10.name: id
p:10.description: Stable identifier, for example dsv:snowflake://acme/stg.orders@17. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:11.name: version
p:11.description: Version as reported by the source system: a number, snapshot id, commit id or hash. Opaque; do not order versions by this value.

p:12.name: generatedAt
p:12.description: When the producing run finished writing this version.

p:13.name: publishedAt
p:13.description: When this version was exposed to consumers. Absent if it was never published or if publication is not tracked.

p:14.name: validFrom
p:14.description: Start of the period in which this is the version consumers should see. Set by ingestion; it may differ from generatedAt, for example for backfills or delayed publication.

p:15.name: validTo
p:15.description: End of that period, exclusive. Absent while the version is current.

p:16.name: invalidatedAt
p:16.description: When this version was declared invalid, for example after a backfill or a deletion request. The version and its lineage are kept.

p:17.name: schemaHash
p:17.description: Hash of the schema of this version.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:4.description: An immutable snapshot of a dataset, produced by at most one run. Runs use and generate dataset versions, which is what makes point-in-time lineage possible. Source versions that no tracked run produced have no generation.

p:18.name: id
p:18.description: Stable identifier, for example col:snowflake://acme/stg.orders.price. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:5.description: A logical column of a dataset, stable across versions. Its versions carry the column-level lineage.

p:20.name: id
p:20.description: Stable identifier, for example colv:snowflake://acme/stg.orders@17.price. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:21.name: name
p:21.description: Column name in this dataset version.

p:22.name: dataType
p:22.description: Data type as reported by the source system, for example NUMBER(10,2).

p:23.name: ordinal
p:23.description: Position of the column in the dataset version.

p:24.name: nullable
p:24.description: Whether the column accepts null values in this version.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:6.description: A column as it exists in one dataset version: name and type at that point in time. Column-level lineage connects column versions, so an assertion always belongs to the run that produced the dataset version.

p:25.name: id
p:25.description: Stable identifier, for example job:airflow://prod/stg_orders. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:26.name: namespace
p:26.description: Namespace of the scheduler or project, for example airflow://prod. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.

p:27.name: name
p:27.description: Name of the job within its namespace. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:7.description: The logical job, stable over time: a dbt model, Airflow task or Spark job. Identified by namespace and name, as in OpenLineage.

p:28.name: id
p:28.description: Stable identifier, for example jobv:airflow://prod/stg_orders@git:ab12. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.

p:30.name: definitionHash
p:30.description: Hash of the effective definition, such as compiled SQL plus pinned dependencies and configuration. Two runs with the same hash ran the same definition.

p:31.name: artifactRef
p:31.description: Reference to the built artifact, for example a container image digest or a dbt manifest.

p:32.name: configRef
p:32.description: Reference to the configuration version that is part of the definition.

p:0.name: id
p:0.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.

n:8.description: An immutable definition of a job: code plus the dependencies and configuration that change what it does. Execution parameters belong to the run, not here. Plays the role of a PROV plan.

p:33.name: id
p:33.description: Stable identifier, for example run:<OpenLineage runId>. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Activity id constraints; the node must carry the Activity label explicitly.

p:35.name: endedAt
p:35.description: When the run reached a terminal status.

p:36.name: status
p:36.description: Normalized status, not an OpenLineage event type. RUNNING: not finished. SUCCESS: finished and all outputs valid. FAILED or ABORTED: finished without valid outputs. PARTIAL: finished with an error, but some outputs were committed and are valid; which ones is recorded on each generated dataset version through validFrom and invalidatedAt. SUCCESS, FAILED, ABORTED and PARTIAL are terminal.

p:37.name: lastEventType
p:37.description: Type of the latest event applied, as sent by OpenLineage.

p:38.name: lastEventTime
p:38.description: eventTime of the latest event applied. Ingestion ignores events older than this value and events that would leave a terminal status.

p:39.name: observedAt
p:39.description: When ingestion last updated this run.

p:40.name: parameters
p:40.description: Effective execution parameters as sanitized JSON, for example the logical date or partition. Never store secrets; use parametersRef for sensitive values.

p:41.name: parametersRef
p:41.description: Reference to the full parameters in a secure store.

p:1.name: id
p:1.description: Stable identifier, unique across all activities.

n:9.description: One execution of a job. Uses input dataset versions and generates output dataset versions. Ingestion folds all events of a run into this node and never moves it from a terminal status back to RUNNING.

p:42.name: id
p:42.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:alice. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.

p:2.name: id
p:2.description: Stable identifier, unique across all agents.

n:10.description: A person responsible for an asset or a run, such as an owner or steward.

p:44.name: id
p:44.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:dbt. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.

p:2.name: id
p:2.description: Stable identifier, unique across all agents.

n:11.description: A piece of software that executes runs, such as an orchestrator or BI server.

p:46.name: id
p:46.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:data-platform. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.

p:2.name: id
p:2.description: Stable identifier, unique across all agents.

n:12.description: A team or organization on whose behalf agents act.

n:13.description: Write-back bookkeeping: one node per write step (owner recipe/step), locked by each run. Technical, never mapped.

p:48.name: role
p:48.description: Role of the input in the run, for example input or lookup.

r:0.description: A run read a dataset version. A run-level fact: it does not say which outputs depend on it.

p:49.name: role
p:49.description: Role of the output in the run, for example output.

r:1.description: A dataset version was written by a run. Each version has at most one generation; source versions have none.

p:50.name: runId
p:50.description: Id of the run the dependency was computed from.

r:2.description: Potential dependency between dataset versions, computed from a run's inputs and outputs (every output of the run to every input). An over-approximation used to speed up traversals, not a proven derivation. Rebuild it from USED and WAS_GENERATED_BY; never edit it by hand.

p:52.name: runId
p:52.description: Id of the run that generated the target-side version. Context for filtering, not a referential integrity guarantee: ingestion must check that this run generated the dataset version of the derived side.

p:53.name: jobVersionId
p:53.description: Id of the job version of that run.

p:55.name: evidenceRef
p:55.description: Reference to the evidence, for example an event id, a manifest path or a parsed query hash.

p:56.name: transformationType
p:56.description: Kind of dependency, as in the OpenLineage column lineage facet. DIRECT: the value is computed from the source. INDIRECT: the source affects the result, for example through a filter, join or grouping.

p:57.name: transformationSubtype
p:57.description: Finer kind, for example IDENTITY, TRANSFORMATION, AGGREGATION, FILTER or JOIN.

p:58.name: expression
p:58.description: Transformation applied, for example price * qty. Descriptive only.

r:3.description: Asserted dataset-level derivation: a named source states that the derived version was computed from the source version. Unlike DEPENDS_ON, it is evidence.

p:60.name: runId
p:60.description: Id of the run that generated the target-side version. Context for filtering, not a referential integrity guarantee: ingestion must check that this run generated the dataset version of the derived side.

p:61.name: jobVersionId
p:61.description: Id of the job version of that run.

p:63.name: evidenceRef
p:63.description: Reference to the evidence, for example an event id, a manifest path or a parsed query hash.

p:64.name: transformationType
p:64.description: Kind of dependency, as in the OpenLineage column lineage facet. DIRECT: the value is computed from the source. INDIRECT: the source affects the result, for example through a filter, join or grouping.

p:65.name: transformationSubtype
p:65.description: Finer kind, for example IDENTITY, TRANSFORMATION, AGGREGATION, FILTER or JOIN.

p:66.name: expression
p:66.description: Transformation applied, for example price * qty. Descriptive only.

r:4.description: Asserted column-level derivation between column versions. The derived column version belongs to a dataset version generated by the run in runId, so assertions from different runs or job versions never mix. The source column version must belong to a dataset version that run used.

r:5.description: A dataset version is a snapshot of exactly one logical dataset.

r:6.description: A logical dataset has a logical column. Each column belongs to exactly one dataset.

r:7.description: A dataset version contains a column version. Each column version belongs to exactly one dataset version.

r:8.description: A column version is a version of exactly one logical column. Ingestion must ensure that the column belongs to the dataset of the column version's dataset version.

r:9.description: A job version is a definition of exactly one logical job.

r:10.description: A run executes exactly one logical job. Always known from the event, even when the code version is not.

r:11.description: The job version a run executed, when known. An LPG shortcut: in PROV-O the plan is attached to the association between an activity and an agent, not to the activity. Ingestion must ensure that the job version is a version of the run's job.

r:12.description: A run used something that another run generated, or was triggered by it.

p:68.name: role
p:68.description: Role of the agent in the run, for example executor or triggeredBy.

r:13.description: An agent was responsible for a run.

p:69.name: role
p:69.description: Role of the agent for the entity, for example owner or steward.

r:14.description: An entity is attributed to an agent, for example a dataset to its owner or steward.

r:15.description: An agent acted on behalf of another agent, for example an orchestrator on behalf of a team.

p:70.name: reason
p:70.description: Why the version was invalidated, for example backfill or deletion request.

r:16.description: A dataset version became invalid because of a run, for example a backfill or a deletion job. Set together with invalidatedAt; the version and its lineage are kept.
